items.claim: When a site bounces the browser to a login prompt, the redirect parameter carried in that login URL (next, retUrl) is the post-login destination the user influences, so it is the parameter to fuzz.
items.body:
When a site bounces the browser to a login prompt, the redirect parameter carried in that login URL (next, retUrl) is the post-login destination the user influences, so it is the parameter to fuzz.

HackTricks reference: find openredirect trick (https://kathan19.gitbook.io/howtohunt/open-redirection/find_openredirect_trick.md)
items.disproof: The redirect parameter refuses external hosts or ignores off-site values and always resolves to a fixed internal path.

sources.quote:
If the site prompts for a login , check the address bar , you may find the login page with a redirect parameter like the following
 * <https://samplesite.me/login?next=accounts/profile>
 * <https://samplesite.me/login?retUrl=accounts/profile>
7.

A 100-continue expectation informs recipients that the client is about to send a (presumably large) message body in this request and wishes to receive a 100 (Continue) interim response if the request-line and header fields are not sufficient to cause an immediate success, redirect, or error response.
An open redirect vulnerability occurs when a website allows user-supplied input to influence the destination of a redirect without implementing proper validation or sanitization measures
